segments.title: Chương 26: 0026 【Nhân Danh Cha, Hiển Thánh】
segments.content:
Yangcheng.

In an unfurnished apartment in a certain residential complex.

Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan were scraping putty; the husband and wife were scraping the ceiling and the walls, respectively.

"Beep, beep, beep, beep..."

The sound of a pager went off.

Chen Xinghua tossed his scraper into the putty bucket and took the pager from his waist to check the message.

"Bring the debt ledger. Son."

Chen Xinghua read it several times, completely failing to understand what it meant.

He jumped down from the scaffolding and held the pager in front of his wife.

Yao Lan didn't know what her son was up to either, but she still said, "Go call him back. I'll handle things here."

After giving a few instructions, Chen Xinghua quickly went downstairs and left the complex.

He didn't go to their rented room to get the debt ledger but directly looked for a nearby public phone to call back. He remembered clearly in his mind who he still owed and how much.

"Liangliang, what do you want me to do with the debt ledger?" Chen Xinghua asked.

Chen Guiliang didn't beat around the bush and said directly, "Dad, I made fifty thousand yuan today."

Chen Xinghua was startled to hear this. "You haven't done anything bad, have you?"

"I sold some business ideas to my cousin's boss's friend," Chen Guiliang explained. "You can call my cousin to check if you don't believe me."

Chen Xinghua fell silent.

It wasn't that he didn't believe his son, but he was too surprised and didn't know what to say.

Chen Guiliang said, "Dad, just read me the names and the amounts. I'll write them down on my end and pay them off directly. If any of the creditors are in Yangcheng right now, you can withdraw money from the card yourself to repay them."

The father and son shared a primary and supplementary card for the same bank account.

Chen Xinghua said:

"There are two working in Yangcheng. I'll take a bus and repay them myself. I'll use the money I saved for your university tuition. That way, I can save on the out-of-town withdrawal fees."

"You write down the rest. Yang Aijun from Group One of our village, I owe him 2360 yuan; Liu Yuejin from Group Four, 2250 yuan. Tang Guangyao from Group Two of Xiafeng Village, 2280 yuan; Liu Gang from Group Two of Xiafeng Village..."

These were all wages in arrears from seven years ago.

Chen Xinghua had been screwed over by a fellow townsman who had subcontracted a project with him, and he had to pay the wages out of his own pocket. Fortunately, the project had already been completed at the time, and a portion of the wages had been paid. The fellow townsman had only run off with the final payment.

For a full seven years, Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan had been working hard to repay the remaining wages.

Chen Guiliang said, "Dad, stop working as a laborer. You and Mom should come back."

"I haven't finished the renovation work I'm on. I'll come home after I'm done at the end of the year," Chen Xinghua said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Alright. I'll wait for you to come back for the New Year."

Chen Xinghua looked at the call duration and, counting the minutes, said, "I'm hanging up now. It'll be charged for another minute if it goes over."

"Goodbye."

The tone of both father and son seemed rather calm.

There was no excitement or joy, no choked sobs or tears, and certainly no need for concerned inquiries.

Surging waves of emotion are often hidden behind a placid exterior.

As Chen Xinghua walked out of the public phone booth, he felt that the sun was particularly brilliant today.

The great mountain that had been weighing on him for seven years was lifted in a single day and thrown into the sea. Even the bones in his body felt several pounds lighter.

He could finally go home for the New Year!

Chen Xinghua hurried back to the house he was renovating, eager to tell his wife the news.

After hearing it, Yao Lan let out a long sigh of relief and quietly walked to the balcony to sit and rest. With her back to her husband, she silently raised a hand to wipe away her tears, but the more she wiped, the more they flowed.

Years of suppression and grievances all turned into tears in that instant.

Yao Lan rested for a few minutes. When the tears stopped flowing, she went back to the living room and continued scraping putty.

Although the debt was paid off, life had to go on.

Her son needed money for university, and their dilapidated house back home needed to be rebuilt.

There were too many things that required money.

After scraping putty for a while, Yao Lan suddenly smiled and said, "Let's finish work early today. I'll go buy some meat. We haven't had meat in a long time."

"Buy some pork, lamb, and fish," Chen Xinghua also broke into a smile. "Let's invite Old Zhang and his wife from next door over too. They were always the ones treating us before; it's our turn to treat them back."

That Chen Guiliang had suddenly earned 50,000 yuan—the couple didn't even ask much about such a major event, not even calling Feng Tao to confirm.

Because they trusted each other, and they trusted their son.

Moreover, they never interfered in their son's affairs, respecting all of his choices.

Out of sight, out of reach.

For seven years they hadn't been home. No amount of interference or questioning would be of any use. Chen Guiliang had been thoroughly left to fend for himself.

Hanging up the phone, he walked out of the phone booth.

Chen Guiliang squatted by the side of the street and began to think about how to handle this.

Even with repaying debts, there were different ways to do it, and the effects they could achieve were completely different.

Relying on distant memories, Chen Guiliang walked towards an old commercial street.

Twenty years from now, this street would be renovated and rebuilt, but at this moment, it was still bustling with people. The shops and stalls on both sides of the street targeted the city's lower-class citizens and farmers who came into the city to shop.

Casual pants printed with a Meteor Garden poster cost only ten yuan a pair, and with a bit of bargaining, you could get them for six or seven yuan.

Chen Guiliang bought a carton of Hongtashan cigarettes, some loose-leaf tobacco, and a few kilograms of roasted cake.

Then he withdrew some cash, took a taxi to the urban-rural fringe, and found a small shop selling televisions.

"How much is this color TV?" Chen Guiliang asked.

The owner received him warmly. "Changhong, a famous brand. If you like it, young man, you can take it for the cost price of 1800. I'll just make a few dozen yuan for my trouble."

Chen Guiliang then asked about the price of a satellite dish, the kind that looked like a one-meter-diameter radar, commonly known as a "satellite pot."

The owner said, "A satellite pot is 500 yuan. Installation is included within two kilometers. If it's more than two kilometers, there's an extra installation fee."

Chen Guiliang cut the price right in half. "I'll give you 2500 for two color TVs. Both have to come with satellite dishes, and you must deliver and install them."

The owner cried foul, "Aiyo, you can't bargain like that, I won't even make back my cost..."

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered with nonsense and turned to walk out.

"Young man, don't go. The price is negotiable," the owner quickly called out to stop him.

Chen Guiliang was already outside the shop.

The owner chased after him and asked, "Where's the delivery?"

"Qianfeng Village, Yaojia Township," Chen Guiliang said.

The owner started complaining again, "Yaojia Township is too far. I wouldn't deliver even with extra money... Hey, don't go! I'll deliver, I'll deliver. You have to pay first!"

Chen Guiliang returned to the shop and quickly paid.

The owner moved the TVs and satellite dishes onto a three-wheeled motorcycle, leaving his wife to watch the shop.

As he started the engine, he was still complaining, saying he was losing money on this deal.

Chen Guiliang stuck a cigarette in his mouth to shut him up, then hopped into the back of the three-wheeler, sitting with the two TVs.

After a long, bumpy ride, the three-wheeler turned from the county road onto a village road.

The village road was even more rugged and uneven, looking as if it could overturn at any moment.

Chen Guiliang silently observed the countryside scenery.

He didn't like it here, didn't like his own village.

Most of his memories of this place weren't very pleasant.

Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan worked hard, paying off the overdue wages one sum at a time. But the villagers who were owed wages directed all their resentment at them. Because the person who ran off with the money had disappeared, cursing a missing person was a waste of effort.

As a result, Chen Guiliang was also looked down upon, and other children were even forbidden from playing with him.

It was understandable for the creditors to act this way, but many villagers who weren't owed money also inexplicably discriminated against Chen Guiliang's family.

Of course, even more villagers were just watching the spectacle, unconcerned as long as it didn't affect them.

It wasn't until more than a decade later that the entire village was demolished for the construction of a high-speed rail line and a new city. Looking at his unrecognizable hometown, watching all the folks from his village relocate, Chen Guiliang finally felt that he had lost something.

In fact, some villagers had been good to him. It was just a shame that the kindness a boy felt was completely overshadowed by a heart full of resentment.

His third cousin, who was of the same generation in the clan but older than his father, had once taken him to the hospital for an emergency on his bicycle in the middle of the night.

Granny Tan, who lived halfway up the mountain across from the paddy fields, would give him candy every time they met on the road, even when he was already in junior high.

There was also Second Uncle Li, who fished as a side job. On his way back from selling fish, he would always deliberately pass by his house and sell him the remaining small fish for next to nothing...

No place is full of only bad people.

"Stop by the bamboo grove up ahead."

Before the three-wheeler came to a complete stop, Chen Guiliang nimbly jumped off and shouted to someone working in the fields by the roadside, "Fourth Uncle Liang, come and give me a hand."

Most of the villagers were related in some way. This "Fourth Uncle Liang" was a distant relative of Chen Guiliang.

Fourth Uncle Liang dropped his hoe and came over, surprised. "Guiliang, you bought a color TV."

Chen Guiliang handed him a pack of Hongtashan. "I bought one for Grandma and one for Grandpa and Grandma on my mom's side."

"Such a filial son!"

Fourth Uncle Liang happily accepted the Hongtashan and eagerly helped the owner carry the TV.

After walking about two or three hundred meters, they had already attracted a crowd of four or five villagers.

A color TV wasn't a rarity.

What was rare was the person buying the TV. Chen Guiliang's family was still in debt!

Right away, a villager quietly ran home. "Quick, go tell Yang Aijun's wife that Chen Guiliang bought two color TVs. Tell her to come over and demand the debt. If she can't get the money, take the TVs as payment!"

His maternal grandfather was in the courtyard tying a broom with sorghum stalks. These brooms could be sold at the market.

Looking at his "resurrected" grandfather, Chen Guiliang's smile became exceptionally bright. "Grandpa, I bought you some loose-leaf tobacco."

"Good."

His grandfather chuckled and continued tying the broom.

Chen Guiliang added, "I also bought you a color TV."

Only then did his grandfather stand up in shock, squinting his presbyopic eyes to look at the people behind Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang said to the owner, "Carry the TV inside and put it in the bedroom."

"This way," his grandfather quickly led the way.

There was no TV stand, so they cleared off a worn-out table and moved it to the bedroom to place the TV on.

More and more villagers, having heard the news, gathered in the courtyard, chatting idly. A few gossipy women stood at a distance, pointing and talking about Chen Guiliang.

A few minutes later, his maternal grandmother and youngest maternal uncle received the news and rushed home from the fields.

As for his eldest maternal uncle and his wife, they had been working in a coastal city all this time, and had even brought their child there to attend a school for migrant workers' children.

"Where is Chen Guiliang? Where is Chen Guiliang?" A village woman came running, who was none other than the wife of the creditor, Yang Aijun.

Chen Guiliang took the initiative to greet her. "Third Auntie Zhu, hello."

The woman, holding the IOU for the wages, grabbed Chen Guiliang's clothes and said, "You have money to buy a color TV, but no money to pay your debts? You have to pay up today, no matter what. If you don't give me the money, I'm taking your TV!"

Chen Guiliang, smiling, took out a thick wad of cash, held it high, and said to the crowd, "My parents have struck it rich. They sent me home to clear all the old debts!"

As soon as he said this, the villagers broke into a buzz of discussion.

Someone asked curiously, "Guiliang, what business did your dad get into to strike it rich?"

Chen Guiliang's lie came out effortlessly. "My parents have a renovation team. Not long ago, they landed a big job. They're doing the renovation for half a building of unfurnished apartments."

Now the villagers were in a complete uproar.

"I always said Chen Xinghua isn't the type to default on his debts. He's been repaying them all these years."

"That's not all. Among all the people from the village who went out to work, he and Shi Qiang were the most successful. He became a foreman in Yangcheng a long time ago."

"Don't mention Shi Qiang. That son of a bitch ran off with all the project funds!"

"Guiliang, is your dad's renovation team looking for people? How much can you make a year working for him?"

"Guiliang, is your dad coming back for the New Year? I want to go out and work next year too. I don't know anything about renovation, but can I be his apprentice?"

"..."

Just a few minutes ago, Chen Guiliang's father was looked down upon by the villagers, having been the subject of countless private jokes over the years.

But in the blink of an eye, he had transformed from a deadbeat into a capable man in the village!

The woman was no longer grabbing Chen Guiliang's clothes, but her tone was still not very pleasant. "It took seven years to pay back the money. If it had been in the bank, the interest would be several hundred yuan."

Bank deposit interest rates in 1996 were close to 10%, only plummeting after the Asian financial crisis.

If you were to calculate the interest strictly, it would be frightening.

But when repaying debts, a little bit of interest was just a token gesture. Getting any at all was an unexpected surprise.

Chen Guiliang counted out an extra two hundred yuan and handed it to the woman along with the principal. "Third Auntie Zhu, this two hundred is the interest. My dad struck it rich, so he'll give what's due. For those we didn't give interest to before, they can all come to my house during the New Year. I'll definitely make up for all the interest!"

The woman's face immediately lit up with joy. She quickly exchanged the IOU for the money and even flattered him, "I knew Brother Chen was an upright man, and very capable. I knew he'd be able to pay back the debt. Guiliang, you're promising too. You'll be a university student in the future, probably going to stay and work in a big city."

To praise the powerful and trample on the weak is human nature.

The reason Chen Guiliang went to all this trouble today was, of course, so that his parents could hold their heads high and be respected when they returned home.

If he had simply paid off the debts, the gossips would still have slandered them!

Therefore, his parents had to have "struck it rich."

Be tough when you're poor, be gracious when you're rich.

At this moment, his maternal grandmother and youngest maternal uncle were grinning from ear to ear. They were surrounded by the onlooking villagers, and all sorts of compliments filled their ears.

This was especially true for the villagers who heard Chen Xinghua had struck it rich and wanted to follow him to do renovation work next year. They were all saying the nicest things, completely forgetting the malicious words they had spoken behind his back.

"Grandma, I bought you your favorite baked cake," Chen Guiliang said, carrying the cake over.

His grandmother was even happier, telling her neighbors, "My grandson is so filial."

The neighbors all chimed in with compliments.

Chen Guiliang smiled along with them, but he felt a little like crying.

Before his rebirth, his maternal grandparents had already passed away one after another.

Especially when his grandfather passed away, he hadn't even been able to see him one last time. When he rushed back to his hometown, he could only go straight to the mourning hall.
